title: Ether Prophesies
summary: Ether, a prophet, comes forth in the days of King Coriantumr and begins to prophesy to the people.

explicit_facts.text: Coriantumr was king over all the land.
Ether was a prophet of the Lord and came forth in Coriantumr’s days to prophesy to the people.
Ether could not be restrained because of the Spirit of the Lord in him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Ether is addressing a group of people.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact place where Ether speaks.
The appearance, clothing, and age of Ether and the people.

narration.text: Ether was a prophet of the Lord

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Spirit as a visible figure or effect; the verse does not describe an appearance.

title: A Day of Exhortation
summary: Ether cries out from morning until sunset, urging the people to believe in God and repent. He teaches that faith brings hope and steadfastness in good works.

explicit_facts.text: Ether cried from morning until sunset, exhorting the people to believe in God unto repentance lest they be destroyed.
Ether taught that faith brings hope for a better world and leads people to steadfastness and good works.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Ether can be shown speaking outdoors during daylight; the verse states the duration but does not specify the precise setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact location, listeners’ reactions, and any objects or structures present.

narration.text: by faith all things are fulfilled
maketh an anchor to the souls of men

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The anchor is a figure of speech and should not be shown as a literal object attached to souls.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict destruction or an anchor as a literal event.

title: Ether’s Unbelieved Prophecy
summary: Ether prophesies great and marvelous things to the people. They do not believe them because they have not seen them.

explicit_facts.text: Ether prophesied great and marvelous things to the people.
The people did not believe what Ether prophesied because they did not see those things.
Moroni addresses the world concerning faith, things hoped for but not seen, and receiving a witness after the trial of faith.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Ether may be shown addressing a group of people.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, the number of people, and their appearances.
How Moroni’s narration is presented visually.

narration.text: Ether did prophesy great and marvelous things unto the people, which they did not believe, because they saw them not.
And now, I, Moroni, would speak somewhat concerning these things;
wherefore, dispute not because ye see not, for ye receive no witness until after the trial of your faith.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Moroni’s words are narration and teaching, not a present-time encounter with Ether.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the prophesied things as visible events.
Do not depict Moroni as physically present with Ether or the people.

title: Faith and Christ’s Appearing
summary: Moroni teaches that Christ showed himself to the fathers after they had faith, and that faith makes hope for unseen things possible.

explicit_facts.text: Christ showed himself to the fathers after he had risen from the dead and after they had faith in him; he did not show himself to the world.
Moroni says Christ has shown himself to the world because of people’s faith and prepared a way for others to partake of the heavenly gift.
Moroni says people may have hope and partake of the gift if they have faith.

unspecified_visual_details: The fathers’ identities, the place of Christ’s appearance, and how the heavenly gift appears.

narration.text: after he had risen from the dead
if ye will but have faith

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This scene presents Moroni’s teaching, not a reenactment of Christ’s historical appearances.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the fathers or Christ as physically present in Moroni’s narrated teaching.

title: Faith Across the Ages
summary: Moroni teaches that faith was involved in the holy order, the giving of the law of Moses, and the fulfillment of God’s more excellent way; he says God does no miracle among people without faith.

explicit_facts.text: People of old were called after the holy order of God by faith.
The law of Moses was given by faith, and God prepared a more excellent way in the gift of his Son, fulfilled by faith.
Moroni says that without faith among the children of men, God can do no miracle among them.

unspecified_visual_details: The identities and appearance of those called to the holy order, and any visual representation of the law or the more excellent way.

narration.text: God can do no miracle among them

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are teachings about faith, not depictions of separate historical events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict miracles, the giving of the law, or the holy order as present-time action.

title: Examples of Faith
summary: The faith of Alma and Amulek caused a prison to tumble to the earth. The faith of Nephi and Lehi wrought a change upon the Lamanites, who were baptized with fire and the Holy Ghost. The faith of Ammon and his brethren wrought a great miracle among the Lamanites. All who wrought miracles did so by faith, before and after Christ.

explicit_facts.text: The faith of Alma and Amulek caused the prison to tumble to the earth.
The faith of Nephi and Lehi wrought a change upon the Lamanites, who were baptized with fire and with the Holy Ghost.
The faith of Ammon and his brethren wrought a great miracle among the Lamanites.
All who wrought miracles did so by faith, both before and after Christ.

unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the prison and the nature of the miracle involving Ammon and his brethren are not specified.

narration.text: it was the faith of Alma and Amulek
wrought so great a miracle among the Lamanites.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses report examples of faith; they do not place these events together in one scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the reported events as happening together or in the present.
Do not invent a visible form for the baptism with fire and with the Holy Ghost or for the unspecified miracle.
Do not assign these words to a speaker not identified in the supplied verses.

title: The Three Disciples’ Promise
summary: Moroni says the three disciples received a promise that they would not taste of death after they had faith, and that people first believed in the Son of God before miracles were wrought.

explicit_facts.text: The three disciples obtained a promise that they should not taste of death, after their faith.
Moroni says miracles were not wrought until after faith, and that people first believed in the Son of God.

unspecified_visual_details: The identities of the three disciples in this account and where they were when they received the promise.

narration.text: they should not taste of death

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is Moroni’s report and teaching, not a new scene showing the disciples.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the disciples or a visible promise as present.

title: Seeing Through Faith
summary: Moroni describes people whose strong faith allowed them to see with their eyes what they had beheld by faith, and who were glad.

explicit_facts.text: Many people before Christ came had exceedingly strong faith and saw with their eyes things they had beheld with an eye of faith; they were glad.

unspecified_visual_details: The people, what they saw, and the setting.

narration.text: they were glad

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse does not identify the things seen or describe their appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent visions, people, or visible objects.

title: The Brother of Jared Sees the Lord’s Finger
summary: God puts forth his finger, and the brother of Jared sees it.

explicit_facts.text: God put forth his finger, and the brother of Jared saw it.
After beholding the finger, the brother of Jared was shown all things by the Lord. This is subsequent to the depicted moment.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The brother of Jared can see the finger God puts forth.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, the appearance of the finger, and God's form beyond the finger.

narration.text: when God put forth his finger he could not hide it from the sight of the brother of Jared

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Verse 21 describes what follows the sight of the finger; it is not part of this visible moment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict God's form beyond the finger.
Do not depict the subsequent showing of all things or a literal veil.

title: Concern About Writing
summary: Moroni reports receiving a command from the Lord and recounts having spoken to him.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni identifies the Lord who commanded him as Jesus Christ.
Moroni reports a promise obtained by his fathers through faith.
Moroni records his own address to the Lord concerning writing, speaking, and the Gentiles.
The brother of Jared is mentioned within Moroni’s reported address, not described as present.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A restrained, non-dramatized presentation can accompany Moroni’s account without reenacting the reported address.
unspecified_visual_details: Moroni’s physical appearance, clothing, and posture.
Setting, lighting, and any writing materials.
The time and physical circumstances of the reported address.

narration.text: And it is by faith that my fathers have obtained the promise that these things should come unto their brethren through the Gentiles; therefore the Lord hath commanded me, yea, even Jesus Christ.
And I said unto him: Lord, the Gentiles will mock at these things, because of our weakness in writing;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: All narration is voiced by Moroni (son of Mormon); the second excerpt introduces his reported speech.
The reported address must not become a new present-tense encounter.
The fathers, their brethren, the Gentiles, and the brother of Jared are mentioned rather than established as physically present.
These verses describe no visible appearance of Jesus Christ or the Holy Ghost.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a visible divine appearance or invent a divine response.
Do not stage the fathers obtaining the promise or the brother of Jared writing.
Do not show the Gentiles actually mocking.
Do not invent a present action of Moroni writing.
Do not literalize powerful words or stumbling over word placement as supernatural or physical events.

title: The Lord Speaks to the Narrator
summary: After the first-person narrator speaks, the Lord speaks to the narrator about mockery, grace, weakness, humility, faith, hope, and charity.

explicit_facts.text: After the narrator has spoken, the Lord speaks to the narrator.
The Lord says fools mock but shall mourn, and that the meek will take no advantage of the narrator’s weakness.
The Lord says he gives people weakness so they may be humble, and promises to make weak things strong for those who humble themselves before him and have faith in him.
The Lord says he will show the Gentiles their weakness and that faith, hope, and charity bring people unto him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The exchange can be depicted without showing the Lord’s form, which the verses do not describe.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and the narrator’s appearance.
Any visible appearance of the Lord.

spoken_dialogue.text: Fools mock, but they shall mourn; and my grace is sufficient for the meek, that they shall take no advantage of your weakness;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: for if they humble themselves before me, and have faith in me, then will I make weak things become strong unto them.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

narration.text: And when I had said this, the Lord spake unto me, saying:

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The fountain in Ether 12:28 is figurative language, not a narrated physical object or location.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the unnamed narrator beyond what these verses establish.
Do not invent a visible appearance for the Lord or depict a literal fountain.
Do not stage the promised strengthening or the Gentiles’ response as events occurring in this exchange.

title: Moroni Is Comforted
summary: Moroni hears words, is comforted, and addresses the Lord. He recounts that the brother of Jared told Mount Zerin to remove and it was removed, and that the Lord manifested himself to his disciples after they had faith and spoke in his name.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni heard words, was comforted, and addressed the Lord.
Moroni says the Lord works unto the children of men according to their faith.
Moroni reports that the brother of Jared told the mountain Zerin to remove, and it was removed.
Moroni says the Lord manifested himself to his disciples after they had faith and spoke in his name.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni may be depicted speaking; his posture and surroundings are not described.
unspecified_visual_details: Moroni’s location and appearance.
The appearance of Mount Zerin and the identities of the disciples.

spoken_dialogue.text: O Lord, thy righteous will be done, for I know that thou workest unto the children of men according to their faith;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Moroni

narration.text: And I, Moroni, having heard these words, was comforted, and said:

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The mountain’s removal and the Lord’s manifestation are recounted events, not present-time action in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the mountain moving or the Lord appearing as present-time action.
Do not attribute the words Moroni heard to a speaker not identified in these verses.

title: Hope and Charity
summary: Moroni recalls the Lord’s words about a prepared place among the Father’s mansions, the Lord laying down his life and taking it again, and charity as necessary to inherit that place. He considers the Gentiles’ charity and their received talent.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni recalls that the Lord prepared a house among the Father’s mansions, where people might have a more excellent hope, and that people must hope to receive an inheritance there.
Moroni recalls that the Lord loved the world, laid down his life, and took it again to prepare a place for the children of men.
Moroni says charity is the Lord’s love for the children of men and that people need charity to inherit the prepared place.
Moroni says the Lord will prove Gentiles who lack charity and take away their talent, giving it to those who have more abundantly.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni may be shown continuing his prayer or reflection; no posture is specified.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the mansions, prepared place, and any representation of talent.

narration.text: except men shall have charity

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Father’s mansions and talent are mentioned in Moroni’s teaching; the verses do not describe them visually.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord’s death, resurrection, mansions, or talent transfer as present action.

title: Prayer for the Gentiles
summary: The narrator prays that the Lord will give the Gentiles grace so they might have charity. The Lord responds, saying the narrator has been faithful and speaking of clean garments, strength, and a prepared place.

explicit_facts.text: The narrator prayed that the Lord would give the Gentiles grace so they might have charity.
The Lord answered the narrator and said the narrator had been faithful.
The Lord said the narrator's garments would be made clean and that, because the narrator had seen their weakness, they would be made strong and sit in a place he had prepared.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The narrator may be depicted praying; the verse does not specify a posture.
The Lord's response may be heard without depicting an appearance.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and the narrator's appearance and posture.
Any visible appearance of the Lord.

spoken_dialogue.text: If they have not charity it mattereth not unto thee, thou hast been faithful; wherefore, thy garments shall be made clean. And because thou hast seen thy weakness thou shalt be made strong, even unto the sitting down in the place which I have prepared in the mansions of my Father.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

narration.text: I prayed unto the Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The clean garments, promised strength, and prepared place are spoken of here; these verses do not narrate their visible fulfillment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the first-person narrator by name from these verses alone.
Do not depict the Lord's appearance, the cleansing of garments, or the narrator sitting in the prepared place.
Do not depict the Gentiles as present at the prayer.

title: Moroni’s Farewell
summary: Moroni bids farewell to the Gentiles and his brethren, saying they will meet before Christ’s judgment-seat and know he has seen Jesus and spoken with him face to face. He commends them to seek Jesus and ends with Amen.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni bids farewell to the Gentiles and his brethren, whom he loves, until they meet before Christ’s judgment-seat.
Moroni says all men will know his garments are not spotted with their blood.
Moroni says he has seen Jesus, who talked with him face to face in his own language.
Moroni says he wrote only a few things because of weakness in writing and commends his readers to seek Jesus.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni may be shown delivering his farewell as narration; the text does not describe a physical audience.
unspecified_visual_details: The place and posture of Moroni, the judgment-seat, and Jesus’s appearance during the past conversation.

narration.text: I would commend you to seek this Jesus
Amen.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Moroni’s past face-to-face conversation with Jesus is mentioned retrospectively and is not a present scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Jesus or the judgment-seat in this farewell scene.
